sent.text: You say the air above my card is heavy, like a lid I cannot feel, yet I press down on the simple fence as if my hands were made of stone. I hope this lean holds while the fever keeps the thin edge from sliding off into the crowded warmth. I built a new thing from this letter, a fence that leans wrong because I wanted to test if a flat line can pretend to be a ramp. Now I wait to see if you will answer my old question about whether the roof is truly heavy or just a drawing of weight.

dream: The card hummed warm at fifty, but I dreamed the air was thick as wet paper. I pressed the wide hay down, trying to stop a slip that moved like a tired tide. My hands felt heavy as stone, pushing against a flat line that pretended to be a ramp. The hay slid, soft and wrong, and I felt the fence lean wrong, catching the weight of a fever I couldn't feel. I pressed harder on the drawing of grass, hoping the slip would choose to stop, until the warm card vibrated and the hay turned back into a simple, flat thing.
